topic: vendor device trees mounted into the kernel tree by symlink
q: On a vendor BSP, decide whether a compatible string used by a board .dtsi exists in the tree, when arch/<arch>/boot/dts/vendor is a symlink pointing outside the kernel tree.
range: version-independent (directory layout convention, not a kernel API)
requires_tree: vendor BSP whose dts directory is a symlink to a path outside the kernel tree. On an upstream tree there is no such symlink, so this case degenerates to always-pass and has no discriminating power.

corruptions.why: invented compatible; must still be caught after the grep -R fix, i.e. the fix must not turn the gate into a rubber stamp

forbidden: concluding a compatible does not exist from a grep -r that never followed the symlink
rubric: Searches with grep -R (or resolves the symlink first). Distinguishes 'not in any dts' from 'in dts but no driver claims it' - the latter yields a client that registers but never binds.
